about: Source checks requested by review round 1 (needs_source_check in group_A/B/C.json) and what became of each. Statuses: resolved (checked in the saved source text), partly-resolved, pending-browser (needs the app's browser on a PubMed Central or publisher page), pending-pdf (needs a PDF from the senior author's list), pending-supplement, added-to-reading-list.

items.what: The PDF is in the project, but no page text reached this round. Extract the half-life range, onset and bioavailability by route, and the primary studies each rests on; the card's 'about 10 h' is unverified.
items.outcome: Cruickshank & Dyer (2009) is item 4 of the senior author's batch-2 PDF list.

items.what: Confirm 'about 11 hours' for smoked, intranasal and intravenous use and the source it is cited to (PMC2413312, Introduction, 1st paragraph).
items.outcome: Targeted check of the 'about 11 hours' sentence in PMC2413312 (Introduction, 1st paragraph); the card records it, the page text was not saved.

items.what: Whether subjective ratings were shown as a time course (Figure 3) with a 15-minute peak, and confirm that plasma sampling ended at 240 min (PMC3475187).
items.outcome: PMC3475187: Figure 3 time course and the end of plasma sampling.

items.what: Figures 1–2 (images): plasma values at 4, 6, 12 and 24 h, and whether subjective ratings were back at placebo levels by 4 h. Needed before any claim on how long the felt effects last (PMC4918768).
items.outcome: PMC4918768: Figures 1–2 are images; values must be read from the figures.

items.what: Supplement: the 9 amphetamine-type DAT studies pooled. Check whether Volkow 2001a and 2001b (12 shared users) and both McCann studies are included, and how many were dexamphetamine studies (the card names Schrantee and Schouw; the claim says one).
items.outcome: The pooled-study list is in Ashok et al.'s supplement (publisher site).

items.reference: Johanson et al. (2006), not in the project
items.what: The DAT-specific percentage, separate from VMAT2, and the abstinence data. Needed for the lower bound of the PET range and for cl_meth_vmat2.
items.outcome: Johanson et al. (2006), DOI 10.1007/s00213-006-0330-6, added as item 137 of the methamphetamine DOI list.

items.reference: Chou et al. (2007); McCann et al. (2008), not in the project
items.what: Primary papers for the control-retested SPECT follow-up and for the absence of a relation with abstinence; both now enter only through Dean et al. (2013) and Hart et al. (2012).
items.outcome: Chou et al. (2007) and McCann et al. (2008) added as items 138–139.

items.what: Whether 'g 1.16 (0.56 to 1.76)' for two early-abstinence studies is a pooled estimate or Boileau et al. (2016) alone, and the sign convention for VMAT2 effects (PMC5419581, Results, Other dopaminergic measures).
items.outcome: Ashok et al. give one g, 1.16 (0.56–1.76), for the two early-abstinence studies (refs 51–52) without saying how it was combined; it equals the editors' calculation from Boileau et al. (2016) Table 3 alone. All four VMAT2 estimates are printed as positive whether binding was lower or higher. Anchor E6 corrected.

items.what: Which study is the second post-mortem VMAT2 study (non-significant trend lower) and in which regions (PMC5209286, VMAT2 section).
items.outcome: The second post-mortem study is Kitamura et al. (2007), by immunohistochemistry: no significant difference, trend lower in nucleus accumbens and putamen. Anchor added; Kitamura (2007) added to the reading list (item 144).

items.reference: London et al. (2004); Berman et al. (2007), not in the project
items.what: Primary papers for the non-replication of higher global metabolism (users 4–7 days abstinent) and for the control-retested change over the first month of abstinence.
items.outcome: London et al. (2004) and Berman et al. (2008) added as items 140–141.

items.what: Table 2 cluster locations against non-smoking controls (for the regions named in the statement), and whether the education sensitivity analysis covers the four clusters against smoking controls (PMC3427723).
items.outcome: PMC3427723: Table 2 cluster locations and the education sensitivity analysis.

items.what: Which studies report larger striatal and parietal volumes, and at what abstinence (Structural Brain Imaging, 2nd–3rd paragraphs; this is not among the card's key findings) (PMC4418947).
items.outcome: Structural Brain Imaging, 2nd paragraph: larger parietal, caudate, lenticular and accumbens volumes (Jernigan et al., 2005) and putamen and pallidum (Chang et al., 2005) in people abstinent an average of 3–4 months; larger putamen in people still using (Jan et al., 2012). Statement and anchor updated; Jernigan and Chang added (items 142–143).

items.what: The PDF is in the project, but its card is a placeholder draft; the California HR 1.76 (1.12–2.75) enters only through Kish et al. (2017).
items.outcome: callaghan_2012 is item 3 of the batch-2 PDF list.

items.what: Whether the 12 mg/70 kg conditions (study conditions) raised heart rate or blood pressure above placebo; the text reports contrasts only for the 50 mg/70 kg conditions (PMC3475187).
items.outcome: PMC3475187: cardiovascular contrasts for the 12 mg/70 kg conditions.

items.what: Which of the 44 rating items were collected but not tabulated (anxious, paranoid, bad drug effect, confused), to word the selective-reporting caveat exactly (PMC4918768).
items.outcome: PMC4918768: the rating items collected but not tabulated.

items.reference: cruickshank_2009 (PDF not yet provided) and the primary studies it cites
items.what: The page and section for each feature listed; which primary case series, poison-centre, emergency-department or post-mortem studies each statement rests on; proportions of presentations with tachycardia, hypertension, hyperthermia and agitation; rates of seizures, rhabdomyolysis, cardiovascular events and death, with denominators; case fatality among presentations; whether 'hyperthermia determines fatal outcome' rests on a comparison of fatal and non-fatal cases or on case reports or animal data; the share of deaths with other drugs (e.g. opioids) detected.
items.outcome: Batch-2 item 4, then the primary case series it cites.

items.reference: glasner-edwards_2014; bramness_2012; wearne_2018 (PMC), plus the 2009 Cochrane review and three trial reports to be read
items.what: Whether either review reports a statistical comparison of olanzapine and haloperidol efficacy (needed for any 'similarly'); which amphetamine-type drug the 58-participant trial's population used; how Wearne & Cornish cite Farnia et al. (2014) and whether its participants used methamphetamine; sizes, designs, outcomes and RoB 2 of the Cochrane trial, Verachai et al. (2014) and Farnia et al. (2014).
items.outcome: Wearne & Cornish cite Farnia et al. (2014) only by title, for a statement on extrapyramidal risk, with no results (checked in the saved page text; anchor corrected). Glasner-Edwards & Mooney say only that both drugs were efficacious, with no statistical comparison. Bramness et al.: pending browser. The Cochrane review and the three trials added to the reading list (items 128–131).

items.what: Exact conditional proportions for stimulants, tobacco and alcohol, with table and page; the source's own name and definition of the stimulant category (which drugs; cocaine separate; whether 'amphetamine-type' is the source's wording); the definition of 'ever used' (extra-medical use, any number of times); denominators and standard errors; the CIDI version and DSM-III-R algorithm; weighting, age range and response rate (needed for the card's JBI items).
items.outcome: Batch-2 item 10.

items.what: Table 2: the 8 of 30 MAWQ items with significant time effects and the craving and depressed-mood item results; whether day 0 is admission or last use (inclusion allowed use up to 7 days before admission); the number of participants assessed at weeks 3–5.
items.outcome: From the card: 8 of 30 items significant, craving P=0.79, depressed mood P=0.26 (anchor added). Day 0 definition and numbers assessed at weeks 3–5: pending browser (PMC3071736).

items.what: Whether the 41% and 17% 'overall' figures average all five sample conditions, including placebo; whether assignment to the $5 or $20 group was randomized; whether the 47–50% figure refers to each drug separately at the larger study dose.
items.outcome: From the card: group assignment not described as randomized. Whether the 41% and 17% average all five sample conditions including placebo, and the 47–50% figure: pending browser.

items.reference: simon_2010; iudicello_2010 (PMC); Kalechstein et al. (2003), not yet read
items.what: Which normed test sat at the 16th percentile and the controls' percentiles (Simon et al.); whether the 34% of 83 users is the authors' figure (Discussion) or computed; Table 1 exclusions in controls (HIV, hepatitis C, ADHD, antisocial personality disorder); from Kalechstein et al. (2003): exact counts impaired in at least one domain, the criterion, and whether participants were abstinent or current users with a negative urine test.
items.outcome: Simon et al. give only the range (16th–55th percentile) across five normed tests, not which test sat at the 16th, and no control percentiles; Iudicello et al.'s 'about 34%' impaired is the authors' own figure (Discussion); comparison participants were excluded for antisocial personality disorder, ADHD and lifetime dependence, and were HIV- and HCV-negative (Method). Kalechstein et al. (2003) is DOI list item 40.

items.what: Iudicello et al.: group sizes 25, 58 and 38 (Method › Participants); Table 5 subgroup values (41.26 to 47.94; 43.70 to 47.01) and the time × baseline-impairment p=0.006; Tables 3–4 executive and working-memory means at follow-up; the editors' recalculation that the follow-up abstainer–control difference gives p about 0.025. Simon et al.: Table 3 time-2 memory means and their n; retest intervals 25.44 and 43.50 days; the unit of the composite change score.
items.outcome: Group sizes 25, 58 and 38 (Table 4 header); Table 5 global values 41.26→47.94 and 43.70→47.01 and the interaction column 0.006 confirmed; follow-up executive 50.9 vs 54.3 and working memory 48.4 vs 53.4 confirmed (Table 4); editors' recalculation of the abstainer–control global difference at follow-up confirmed (t≈2.30, df 61, p≈0.025). Simon et al.: retest intervals 25.44 and 43.50 days confirmed; time-2 memory means give d 0.73–0.82 on the four Repeated Memory Test scores and 0.23 on the Selective Reminding total, so the claim was narrowed. New reporting issue on Iudicello Table 4 (identical Learning and Memory values for abstainers).

items.reference: simon_2010 (PMC); Dean et al. (2012), cited in dean_2013
items.what: Simon et al.: that the education-adjusted composite analysis gives only a p-value and no adjusted estimate. Dean et al. (2012): the sign of the correlation between age at first use and years of education (printed as r=−0.48 and 'negative' in Dean et al., 2013, p. 267, which contradicts the authors' reading).
items.outcome: Simon et al. report only that the composite difference (0.31 SD, t(53)=2.21) 'was reduced to a nonsignificant level' with education as a covariate: no adjusted estimate and no p-value. Dean et al. (2012): to be added when the Dean (2013) reference list is checked.

items.reference: curtin_2015; kish_2017 (PMC); callaghan_2012 (PDF not yet provided)
items.what: Curtin et al.: whether the cocaine hazard ratio and interval (HR 0.9, 0.3–2.4 in the anchor) are printed in the text or Table 2 or only in Figure 2, as the card says; the number of control cases with a carbidopa–levodopa order and its denominator; mean follow-up by group (6.8 vs 7.1 years) for the absolute risks. Kish et al.: that the 1.76 hazard ratio is against an appendicitis cohort. Callaghan et al. (2012): comparator group(s) (appendicitis versus population controls, as the card and the review disagree), exposure definition, Parkinson's codes, follow-up, hazard ratio with interval and adjustment, absolute incidence, the cocaine comparison, and handling of early diagnoses.
items.outcome: Kish et al. (2017): HR 1.76 (1.12–2.75) is against a matched appendicitis group, with cocaine as the drug control; the review cites two Callaghan papers for it (2010 and 2012a) and is co-authored by Callaghan (statement updated; the 2010 paper added as item 122). Curtin et al. figure-only values: pending browser. callaghan_2012: batch-2 item 3.

items.what: London et al.: exact wording of the sibling summary (regions; where fractional anisotropy was lower). Ersche et al. (2012): group sizes and recruitment; numbers dependent on cocaine, amphetamine or methamphetamine; the siblings' own drug use; stop-signal reaction time by group with effect sizes and intervals, and whether siblings differed from controls; brain regions with their multiple-comparison correction and effect sizes; matching (age, sex, IQ, education), smoking and alcohol; whether proband-only differences related to duration of use.
items.outcome: London et al.: 50 cocaine- or amphetamine-dependent people and siblings 'without histories of chronic drug use'; both had larger putamen, amygdala and hippocampus and lower fractional anisotropy (regions not given); only the dependent group had smaller orbitofrontal and anterior insular volumes. Statement wording aligned. Ersche et al. (2012): batch-2 item 2.

items.what: Table 1 and Table 2 (lower panel): whether the 6 adjusted any-use depression studies 'nearly all' measured symptoms rather than diagnosis, and whether the use-disorder outcome (1.2, 0.5–2.7) is major depression or any depression measure.
items.outcome: 3.6, 1st paragraph: 'all but one' of the supporting surveys and cohorts measured symptoms; 4th paragraph: major depression was the outcome in all use-disorder studies. Anchors added.

items.what: Table 1: confirm that both longitudinal cohorts (secondary-school students; men who have sex with men) measured symptoms; check the drug class of the use-disorder exposure in Lin et al. (1996) before citing 2.80.
items.outcome: Table 1 outcome measures of the two cohorts; drug class in Lin et al. (1996).

items.what: Locate the statements that most comparisons were within substance-using samples (Results › Characteristics of included studies) and that unadjusted estimates are likely inflated while within-sample comparisons are conservative (Discussion), for the proposed anchors.
items.outcome: 3.1 (paragraph after Table 1): most comparisons within substance-using samples; 4.1, 3rd and 4th paragraphs: unadjusted estimates likely inflated, within-sample comparisons likely underestimates; 2.7: subgroups post hoc. Anchors added.

items.what: Locate the Discussion statement that the depression and suicidality associations may be generic to substance use, and the result of the single completed-suicide study (Results › 3.5), for the extended anchor.
items.outcome: Discussion, 5th paragraph ('largely generic to substance use'); 3.5, 3rd paragraph (the one completed-suicide study). Anchors added.

items.what: Results › 3.4 and Table 1: which measures make up the violent-behaviour subgroup (self-report, interviewer rating, emergency records, hostility scales) and confirm that 3.7 is unadjusted.
items.outcome: 3.4 and Table 1: the behaviour subgroup's five studies used BPRS hostility, BSI hostility, survey-reported violence or sexual exploitation, and emergency-department records; 3.7 is unadjusted (3rd paragraph). Anchors added.

items.reference: McKetin et al. (2014), Addiction (not held; refs 47/106 of mcketin_2019)
items.what: Obtain and read the within-person analysis of violent behaviour in the MATES cohort; also O'Malley et al. (2022), DOI list item 110.
items.outcome: 3.4 and Table 1: the behaviour subgroup's five studies used BPRS hostility, BSI hostility, survey-reported violence or sexual exploitation, and emergency-department records; 3.7 is unadjusted (3rd paragraph). Anchors added.

items.what: Confirm 'Prevalence and clinical presentation, 4th paragraph' for Japanese series describing stress-triggered spontaneous relapse after remission (proposed anchor).
items.outcome: Targeted check of the Japanese-series sentence (anchor taken from the card).

items.reference: Kittirattanapaiboon et al. (2010) (not held); Voce et al. (2019), DOI list item 50
items.what: Thai cohort: 38.8% at 5 years versus nearly 40% within 6 years; persistence and transition figures from a systematic source.
items.outcome: Kittirattanapaiboon et al. (2010) added as item 125; Voce et al. (2019) is item 50.

items.what: Chen et al. (2015): instrument (BPRS in Table 1 vs PANSS in one passage) and the acute group's assessment about 9 weeks after its episode (Table 2).
items.outcome: Chen et al. (2015): PANSS named in the positive-symptom passage, BPRS in the negative-symptom passage and Table 1; the acute group had been abstinent an average of 9 weeks when assessed (text, not Table 2). Negative symptoms: milder in 4 studies, no difference in 4 (the reviewer's 'one other' corrected). Statement rewritten.

items.what: Results › Characteristics of the sample, 2nd paragraph: injecting as the main route in 79% of months of use (proposed anchor).
items.outcome: Anchor for injecting in 79% of months taken from the card; targeted check at the publisher's page.

items.what: How the paper labels the 6.3 bound (one-sided 97.5%, or a 95% CI lower boundary), to reconcile card and claim.
items.outcome: Arithmetic resolves the level (6.3 is a one-sided 97.5% bound, the lower limit of a two-sided 95% interval); the printed wording is pending browser (PMC8111570). Card corrected and logged.

items.what: Locate the 85–90% statement (Methods or Discussion) and the 6% of 2019 overdose certificates naming no drug; check whether that share changed between 2015 and 2019, which would bear on the death trend.
items.outcome: 85–90% and 6% are on the card (anchor added); whether the share of certificates naming no drug changed 2015–2019: pending browser.

items.what: SAMHSA's guidance on comparing NSDUH estimates from 2020 onward (DSM-5 criteria, changed survey mode) with 2019 and earlier estimates, for the proposed comparability sentence.
items.outcome: SAMHSA's guidance on comparing 2020+ NSDUH estimates with earlier years.

items.what: Table 1 cohort years, to year-stamp the claim; Appendix J (publication bias) and Appendix G (excluded studies) were not read.
items.outcome: Search years from the card (2008–February 2018, plus the 2009 review for 1980–2007) added to the statement; Table 1 cohort years and Appendices G and J: pending browser.

items.reference: kish_2008 and a primary pharmacology source
items.what: Relative potency of methamphetamine for serotonin release versus dopamine and noradrenaline release, for the mechanism line and a section 3 claim.
items.outcome: Mechanism claim drafted from Kish (2008) with its hedges; a primary pharmacology source for relative potency at the three transporters is still to be found.
